description: Shared TS/Kotlin conformance vectors for the schedule-runtime policy-acceptance gate (SchedulePolicyValidator / ScheduleRuntimeState). This layer sits IN FRONT OF the evaluator: it decides which locally-persisted SchedulePolicyV1 record the evaluator should be fed for a given evaluation, distinguishing CURRENT / STALE_REMOTE / INVALID / EPOCH_STALE / NO_ACCEPTED_POLICY (mission section 11). Unlike schedule-conformance-v1.json this has no pre-existing backend/src/schedule reference implementation -- it is new logic invented for this mission, defined once here and mirrored by a same-semantics reference implementation in backend/test/runtime-schedule-conformance (test-only, NOT backend/src) and the production Kotlin implementation in android/.../runtime/schedule.
notes: effectivePolicy is the policyId+policyRevision the evaluator should actually be fed for this tick; it is expressed here as one of null | "candidate" | "lastKnownGood" (never a full inline policy) to keep vectors compact -- conformance tests resolve those tags against the vector's own candidatePolicy / lastKnownGoodPolicy fields.

Fail-safe rule under test throughout: INVALID and EPOCH_STALE never resolve to an *unrestricted* outcome merely by returning null when a previously-accepted-valid policy is available as a fallback -- they only resolve to null when nothing has ever been validly accepted, which is behaviorally identical to NO_ACCEPTED_POLICY at the evaluator (empty windows => ALLOWED), never to a smaller/different restriction set.

STALE_REMOTE never changes effectivePolicy from the candidate -- it is a labeling-only state for honest parent-facing sync-freshness UI; enforcement is unaffected by connectivity per PCA-4 offline-first.

policyAcceptanceVectors.description: No candidate policy has ever been locally accepted.
A structurally valid, unexpired, epoch-matching candidate policy while online is CURRENT.
Offline, but the last successful sync is well inside the staleness threshold -- still CURRENT, not STALE_REMOTE.
A candidate policy whose epochs exactly equal the device's current known epochs is CURRENT -- "behind" requires strictly less than, not not-equal.

Offline with a last sync older than the staleness threshold is STALE_REMOTE for UI purposes, but the candidate policy is still the effective (fully enforced) one -- offline duration alone never relaxes control.
Offline with no recorded lastPolicySyncAtUtc at all (freshness genuinely unknown) is also STALE_REMOTE, and still fully enforces the candidate.
A candidate whose window configuration fails structural validation is INVALID, but the runtime fails safe onto the last previously-accepted-valid policy rather than going unrestricted.

The same malformed candidate with no fallback available at all resolves to a null effective policy (behaviorally identical to NO_ACCEPTED_POLICY at the evaluator), never a crash and never a fabricated restriction.

A structurally valid candidate whose own expiresAt has passed is INVALID (its stated validity period is over), and fails safe onto the last-known-good policy rather than defaulting to unrestricted merely because it expired.
A candidate with an expiresAt strictly in the future is not expired -- still CURRENT.

A structurally valid candidate authored under an older trustSetEpoch than the device currently knows (e.g. a device revoke happened since) is EPOCH_STALE, and fails safe onto the last-known-good policy.

A candidate behind on keyEpoch with NO last-known-good fallback available still fails safe onto ITSELF (its windows are structurally fine, just possibly trust-stale) rather than opening up to unrestricted.

revisionAcceptanceVectors.description: The very first accepted revision for a family/child is always acceptable.
A strictly greater revision than the previously accepted one is acceptable.
An equal revision (e.g. an idempotent redelivery) is not a new acceptable update at this local merge check.
A lower (stale/out-of-order) revision than the previously accepted one is rejected.
